decision: Reproduced on trunk at a340f81 (1180x820 and 820x1180, level 1, real GPU ?q=high, CDP touch). A drop is judged by the piece centre over the drawn band only, so it hits inside the band and misses a few px outside. Landscape bands (piece centre y): ice 445-471, gap 471-474, rock 474-511; portrait ice 618-636, gap, rock 638-664. Every point with the piece centre inside a band hit (band centres and points 1.5 px inside each edge: 6 of 6 in each orientation); 4 px outside every edge missed.
why: The piece draws 19 to 25 px above the finger (lift), so a finger placed on the ice band centre leaves the piece over the planet: landscape finger on ice centre -> piece y 437 -> miss; portrait finger on ice centre -> piece y 612 -> miss. Finger on rock centre -> piece y 467 -> hit on ICE (a wrong answer counted); portrait -> piece in the gap, miss. A miss floats home silently.
result: miss reproduced; build the feedback and the reach

decision: A drop picks the slot visible nearest the piece's drawn centre within 3% of the screen's short side (about 25 px on an iPad), looked up by 49 probe lines of sight (the centre, then 8 directions at 6 distances), the same call for the light and the drop
why: Finger-on-band drags put the piece 19 to 25 px above the band (lift), so a finger on the ice band lands on the planet; a reach of about 25 px covers that and is less than the 130 px from the piece's home to the rock ring, so a lift without a move never lands. One call for light and drop keeps lit == picked
evidence: trunk finger-aim logs: landscape piece y 437 vs ice band 445-471; portrait 612 vs 618-636

decision: Drop test is analytic: the line of sight meets the ring plane, slotAtPoint(slot table: radii, arc) names the band, the planet is a ball that hides it
why: First version raycast the tap meshes and the planet sphere (3072 triangles): 5.7 ms per call at level 3 on this machine, too slow for every pointer move on an iPad. Analytic: 0.13 ms worst case (miss), 0.025 ms inside. A test checks the analytic bands against the tap meshes at 2000+ ring points
evidence: measured in the browser at ?q=high, level 3, 4 slots (scratchpad cost.mjs)

decision: The plan says leave the planet out of the drop rays. Kept as a hider only, never an answer
why: Without it a piece drawn on the upper planet would land on the back of the ring hidden behind it (a test pins this). It is never an answer and a drop on the planet floats home
evidence: tests/saturn-flow.test.js 'on the planet, where the back of the ice ring is hidden behind it'; mutation without the planet fails it

decision: Light = the slot's own tap band drawn additive gold at 0.55 while the piece is over it; a drop on no ring glows every slot at 0.5 for 0.6 s and ticks; drag.js gets an optional onMove hook
why: The tap band is the exact area that takes the drop, so the light shows the true target and the same for the right and wrong ring (rule 2). A neutral flash on every ring shows nothing of the answer. Pup Delivery defines no onMove: tests/input/drag.test.js

decision: The piece is drawn over the rings and the planet (depthTest off, renderOrder 4)
why: It flies on a plane below the ring plane, so the opaque ring hid it when she held it over a ring and the planet hid it when she dragged up: held-point screenshots of the head build before this change (the piece drawn as on trunk) showed the crystal almost gone over the ice band and gone over the planet
evidence: shots of ice centre and planet middle before and after, scratch run shots-try (deleted after reading)
